statement: Across preregistered short-horizon, long-only contest scenarios, a feasible policy selected to maximize simulated P(final_rank = 1) achieves a higher first-place probability than a policy selected only to maximize expected terminal return.
rationale: The project objective is rank-based. Existing competition research motivates testing whether terminal-rank objectives differ from expected-return objectives, but transfer to Actinver is unproven.

falsification_plan.approach: Lock opponent/state generation, evaluation paths, and final contest scenarios before policy selection; audit every information timestamp.
Compare rank outcomes across distinct market and opponent regimes; reject gains concentrated in one regime.
Remove or block-resample dominant contest periods and test whether the difference survives without a single lucky path.
Vary nearby risk, concentration, time-remaining, and opponent-mixture settings without choosing on the final scenario set.
Apply only verified eligible identifiers, instrument-level liquidity, M3 fill constraints, and no-short/concentration rules.
Use versioned Actinver fees plus calibrated slippage and execution/no-fill scenarios; include sensitivity ranges.
Report uncertainty intervals over independent contest paths and opponent populations; do not infer precision from Monte Carlo count alone.
Record all policy and opponent-generator variants; use a locked final scenario set and adjust for search over variants.
